flags.summary: Prospect disclosed several years of progressively worsening low back pain now spreading up the spine, plus a new radicular symptom down the left leg he attributes to the sciatic nerve, while under active biweekly physiotherapy — and was sold a $6,000 loaded ballistic kettlebell programme with no question asked about clinician clearance.
evidence: I've had lower back problems for a while now, for a number of years that as I've... I've older and I haven't been focusing on taking care of that. It's been progressively getting worse and has now started to, I guess, affect other parts of my body.
Everything's kind of locked up because it's protecting itself. And that has now caused my mid back to start to feel pain and ache and working its way up into my neck, my shoulder.

As of late, I've got this other thing, I'm pretty sure it has to do with my sciatic nerve. I've kind of got this pain on the top of my left hip that's kind of going down my leg now, and I'm just like, where did that come from?
I see a PT every like two weeks, which is very helpful.
I have really bad posterior pelvic tilt, so everything is tilted back
when I wake up, man, I'm stiff and I gotta, you know, slow... I do have to be mindful of, you know, if I'm picking up my kid wrong or picking up something not in the right way, I'll feel it

flags.summary: The rep offered his own mechanistic explanation of the prospect's spinal pain and positioned strength training as the correction to the approach of the physiotherapist currently treating him.
evidence: Rep: because it's not only, like you can stretch a lot because a lot of people are saying, oh, I'm stiff, I need to stretch a lot. No, you need to get stronger because your muscles, like your case is the same thing. Like, okay, you're lifting heavy things, but your muscles are not prepared for that

Rep: You're talking with a guy that was born with hip degeneration... And for many years, I was just having aching pains. And I thought, it's just muscles. And it turned out after 20 years that these are not muscles. This is just joint pain, yeah? But kettlebells helped me with that too
Rep: remember how you told me that like you have this lower back pains and waking up stiff and so on. So this is the thing that we're going to address at first
Pat Soldow: I see a PT every like two weeks, which is very helpful.

flags.summary: An absolute efficacy claim was made to a prospect with progressive spinal pain and suspected sciatic involvement, framing any failure to get results as the client's own fault.
evidence: Rep: So the only way you don't get results in this program is if you choose not to show up, but based on everything you told me, that's not who you are, right?
Pat Soldow: No, it's it's not. Like I said, I... I'm ready to make this commitment
Rep: Trevor has been doing that for six years, over 1,000 satisfied clients.

flags.summary: The rep refused a twenty-four-hour payment deferral from a prospect awaiting house-sale proceeds, applied calendar-scarcity pressure, and ran two consumer credit applications on the call instead — one of which was declined.
evidence: Pat Soldow: It will probably be credit. Can I let you know at the time of the call? — Rep: No. We need to go through that right now.

Rep: So here's the thing. Because we're working with a financing provider. Have you heard about Klarna?... we work with Paiva Financing, so you can put it on that, so we can do it from the get-go right now. If that's an option right now, let's just do that.
Pat Soldow: Does this have to happen right this second? I mean, is there couple days or tomorrow going to delay or is that like a big deal?
Pat Soldow: I mean, I can just pay cash. As as I close on my house, but if you've got numbers that go along with your calls and you've got to close on a call, like...
Rep: The thing is that my calendar is pretty packed, so whenever I have to reschedule with someone, I have to kick out someone, too.
Pat Soldow: Is this PayPal financing? Yep. They could not approve my application.

flags.summary: A $3,000 six-month extension was quoted as a 'top-up' to the $6,000 programme; the authorised 12-month tier of $9,000 was never presented as an option at the point of offer, only $6,000 was named.
evidence: Rep: that's a total investment of $6,000, and we're off.
Rep: So, you can top that up for, for 12 months, if you would like to.
Rep: Additional 3K, so to top that up, yeah? But you don't, like, in my opinion, six months for you, it's going to be enough.
Pat Soldow: Okay, so six grand for the program, six months for the transformation, yep.
